title: Rosalind and the Contact
premise: Silas Quintana has spent six years as a ghost-for-hire, guarding witnesses and secrets for clients who pay in cash and deniability. When she finds the safe house she's been living in listed online — interior photos included, her own silhouette blurred but recognizable in one shot — she realizes someone sold her location to flush out the witness she's protecting: a former cryptographer holding proof that three governments jointly ran an illegal rendition program. Hunted by a meticulous assassin named Voss and betrayed by the agency that hired her, Silas must move the witness across a border whose checkpoint shift schedule is the only window they'll ever get. She survives by trading the one thing she swore never to give up — her real name and the memory of the family she erased to become invisible — and ends the book testifying anonymously while finally, quietly, going home.
about_author: Felix Sandoval is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian convoys who writes thrillers drawn from the border towns and back channels he once navigated. He lives under no particular alias, which he considers his most radical act.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Silas Quintana, POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., Silas finds the safe house photographed room by room — including the go-bag by the door. Her routine of paranoia pays off in one sickening jolt. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety shatters; she wakes the witness, Mara Voss-adjacent cryptographer Ilsa Brandt, and starts the clock.

chapters.title: Six Years of Nobody
chapters.summary: Silas, POV, flashback-woven. As they pack, we learn how Silas erased herself after a protection detail went wrong in Ciudad Juárez. The emotional beat is grief disguised as competence — she's good at disappearing because she already mourned herself.

chapters.title: Client Zero
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Ilsa explains what she carries: decryption keys proving a joint rendition program across three governments. She doesn't trust Silas, and says so. Beat: wary alliance formed under duress; both women are keeping something back.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The assassin Voss reviews the listing photos with professional admiration — whoever leaked them wanted Silas flushed, not killed yet. Beat: cold dread established; Voss is patient, methodical, and knows Silas's old callsign.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Her agency contact Dane insists the leak is contained and offers a new safe house. Silas notices the address matches a pattern from her erased past. Beat: betrayal seeded; she lies to Dane about their route.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Planning the crossing: the border checkpoint shifts change at 22:40, leaving a nine-minute gap in coverage. Beat: hope with a deadline; the nine minutes becomes the book's ticking clock.

chapters.title: Burned Safe House
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Voss searches the abandoned safe house and reconstructs Silas's habits from wear marks on the floor. Beat: intimacy of pursuit — the hunter knows her better than her allies do.

chapters.title: Freight and Favors
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. She cashes every favor she has, including a smuggler named Okonkwo who owes her from Juárez. Beat: the cost of survival made literal — each favor costs a piece of her anonymity.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Buried
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Confession on the road: Ilsa helped build the encryption the program used. Beat: guilt meets pragmatism; Silas realizes her client is also a perpetrator seeking absolution through exposure.

chapters.title: Dane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dane, POV. Revealed: the agency sold the listing to force Ilsa into the open for all three governments at once. Beat: scale of conspiracy lands; Silas was never the target, just the door.

chapters.title: The Motel With Two Exits
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. A night stop where Voss nearly takes them; Silas escapes through a laundry corridor using a trick from her old life. Beat: first direct contact with Voss — he calls her by her real name.

chapters.title: Rosalind
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Shaken, Silas unpacks the name she buried: Rosalind Quintana, sister, daughter, the woman who existed before the go-bag. Beat: identity crisis peaks; invisibility starts feeling like death rather than safety.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. They copy the archive to three dead-drops so no single government can bury it. Beat: strategy as defiance; the women stop running and start choosing targets.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Price
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Okonkwo agrees to drive them to the checkpoint but demands Silas surrender the fake passport that could save her later. Beat: sacrifice compounding; belonging purchased with future risk.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Voss intercepts Dane, learns the route, and lets Dane be arrested — tying off loose ends. Beat: dread deepens; the hunter now holds the schedule itself.

chapters.title: Nine Minutes
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The checkpoint approach at dusk; everything goes wrong early when a patrol spot-checks traffic. Beat: peak tension; the plan begins dying in real time.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Silas and Voss. In the nine-minute gap, Voss corners them at the crossing; Silas trades the truth — her testimony, her name on record — for Ilsa's passage. Beat: climax; survival redefined as exposure, not escape.

chapters.title: After the Border
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Ilsa crosses; Silas doesn't. From the far side, Ilsa activates the dead-drops. Beat: grief and resolve entwined; the mission continues without its protector.

chapters.title: Interview Room Four
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Detained, Silas gives a full statement — Rosalind Quintana, on the record, naming names. Beat: catharsis through confession; memory becomes weapon instead of wound.

chapters.title: Voss's Report
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Voss files his report omitting the crossing, having decided some clients deserve to survive. Beat: unexpected grace; even the assassin pays a price for what he witnessed.

chapters.title: The Program Unravels
chapters.summary: Alternating brief POVs. The dead-drop data detonates across three capitals; hearings begin; Dane cooperates to save himself. Beat: vindication without triumph — the machine bleeds but isn't destroyed.

chapters.title: Going Home
chapters.summary: Rosalind, POV. Months later, she visits her mother's house under her real name, go-bag unpacked for the first time in six years. Beat: resolution; belonging reclaimed at the price of everything she used to hide behind.
